detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
Fixed and verified on the board.

## Root cause

`report_task` and `queue` both used the *same* stack buffer, aliased through a pointer:

```c
char line[48];                       // one buffer, reused every iteration
...
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);     // queues the pointer, not the text
```

The queue only stored `char *` values that all pointed at `sensor_task`'s single `line` buffer. By the time `report_task` drained an entry (it also `vTaskDelay(30)`s before printing), the sensor loop had already `snprintf`'d the next reading into that same buffer. Every queued pointer therefore resolved to whatever text was written last — the final reading of the burst. That is exactly the observed output: each burst printed e.g. `seq=44` five times with one temperature, so readings were duplicated/lost and temperatures didn't match their seq.

A secondary issue: `QUEUE_LEN` (4) was smaller than `FIFO_BURST` (5), so a full burst couldn't be buffered without a blocking/timeout send.

## What I changed (`main/main.c`)

- Queue now stores the line **by value** (`xQueueCreate(QUEUE_LEN, LINE_LEN)` with `LINE_LEN 48`); `sensor_task` passes `line` to `xQueueSend`, which copies it, and `report_task` receives into its own `char msg[LINE_LEN]`.
- `QUEUE_LEN` raised 4 → 8 so an entire 5-reading burst fits without dropping or blocking.

Report line format (`report seq=<n> temp=<t>`), burst size (5) and burst interval (500 ms) are unchanged.

Verified serial output after flashing now counts `seq=0, 1, 2, 3, ...` in order, each with its own temperature.
